concepts.name: Accuracy
concepts.definition: The share of predictions that are correct; misleading when classes are imbalanced.

concepts.name: Addition Rule
concepts.definition: When alternatives are mutually exclusive, the number of outcomes is the sum of the counts.

concepts.name: Antiderivative
concepts.definition: A function whose derivative is the given function; differentiation run backwards.

concepts.name: Applications of the Definite Integral
concepts.definition: Using integration to compute areas, volumes, lengths and accumulated quantities.

concepts.name: Artificial Neuron
concepts.definition: A unit computing a weighted sum of inputs followed by a non-linear activation.

concepts.name: Averaging and Majority Vote
concepts.definition: The simplest combination rules: average the predicted numbers, or take the most frequent predicted class.

concepts.name: Backpropagation
concepts.definition: Computing the gradient of the loss with respect to every weight by applying the chain rule backwards through the layers.

concepts.name: Bagging
concepts.definition: Training each member on a bootstrap resample to decorrelate their errors and cut variance.

concepts.name: Baseline
concepts.definition: The trivial predictor any real model must beat before its score means anything.

concepts.name: Bayes' Rule
concepts.definition: The formula inverting a conditional probability, turning likelihood and prior into posterior.

concepts.name: Big-O Notation
concepts.definition: A notation bounding a function's growth from above up to a constant factor, used to compare rates of change.

concepts.name: Adaptive Boosting
concepts.definition: Fitting members in sequence, each concentrating on the examples its predecessors got wrong.

concepts.name: The Number of Elements in a Finite Set
concepts.definition: Counting a finite set, including the inclusion–exclusion correction for overlapping parts.

concepts.name: Cartesian Product
concepts.definition: The set of all ordered pairs drawn from two sets, the formal model of independent choices.

concepts.name: Cauchy Mean Value Theorem
concepts.definition: A two-function generalisation of the mean value theorem, the basis for L'Hôpital's rule.

concepts.name: Classification
concepts.definition: Supervised prediction of a discrete class label.

concepts.name: Matrix of a System of Linear Equations
concepts.definition: The matrix that holds the coefficients of an SLE, optionally augmented with the right-hand side column, so that the system can be manipulated as a single object instead of as separate equations.

concepts.name: Combination
concepts.definition: A selection of objects where order does not matter; the binomial coefficient counts them.

concepts.name: Combinatorics in Probability Problems
concepts.definition: Computing probabilities of equally likely outcomes by counting favourable and total cases.

concepts.name: Conditional Probability
concepts.definition: The probability of an event given that another has occurred, obtained by restricting the event space.

concepts.name: Confusion Matrix
concepts.definition: The table of predicted against actual classes, from which most classification metrics are derived.

concepts.name: Continuity on a Closed Interval
concepts.definition: A function is continuous on a closed interval when small changes of argument produce small changes of value throughout it, which guarantees strong global properties.

concepts.name: Convergence of a Series
concepts.definition: A series converges when its partial sums approach a finite limit.

concepts.name: Tests for Convergence
concepts.definition: The standard criteria — comparison, ratio, root, integral — for deciding convergence without summing.

concepts.name: Convergent Sequence
concepts.definition: A sequence that has a finite limit; such sequences are bounded and their limits respect arithmetic.

concepts.name: Convexity
concepts.definition: A function is convex when its graph lies below its chords; convexity is what makes minimisation well behaved.

concepts.name: Convolutional Operation
concepts.definition: Sliding a shared small filter across the input so that the same local pattern is detected anywhere.

concepts.name: Cross-Validation
concepts.definition: Rotating the held-out fold over the data to get a more stable performance estimate.

concepts.name: The Curse of Dimensionality
concepts.definition: In high dimensions data becomes sparse and distances lose contrast, undermining methods that rely on proximity.

concepts.name: Data Augmentation
concepts.definition: Enlarging the training set with label-preserving transformations of existing examples.

concepts.name: Data Compression
concepts.definition: Representing data with fewer numbers while preserving what matters.

concepts.name: DBSCAN
concepts.definition: Density-based clustering that finds arbitrarily shaped clusters and labels sparse points as noise.

concepts.name: Decision Tree
concepts.definition: A predictor that splits the feature space by recursive threshold questions.

concepts.name: Deep Learning
concepts.definition: Learning with many-layered networks that build their own representations of the input.

concepts.name: Definite Integral
concepts.definition: A number attached to a function on an interval, interpretable as signed area under its graph.

concepts.name: Derivative
concepts.definition: The instantaneous rate of change of a function, defined as the limit of its difference quotient.

concepts.name: Determinant
concepts.definition: A single number computed from a square matrix that reports whether the matrix is invertible: a zero determinant means the transformation collapses space and cannot be undone.

concepts.name: Geometric Meaning of the Determinant
concepts.definition: For a 2×2 matrix the determinant is the signed area of the parallelogram spanned by its columns, so its magnitude is the area scaling factor and its sign records whether orientation is flipped.

concepts.name: Differentiable Function
concepts.definition: A function possessing a derivative at every point of an interval; differentiability implies continuity.

concepts.name: Differential of a Function
concepts.definition: The linear part of a function's increment, the formal expression of local linear approximation.

concepts.name: Differentiation Rules
concepts.definition: The algebraic rules — sum, product, quotient and chain — that let derivatives be computed without returning to the limit.

concepts.name: Domain of Convergence
concepts.definition: The set of arguments for which a power series converges.

concepts.name: Dropout
concepts.definition: Randomly disabling units during training so the network cannot rely on any single path.

concepts.name: Elementary Row Operations
concepts.definition: The three reversible moves on a matrix — swapping two rows, scaling a row by a non-zero number, and adding a multiple of one row to another — that change the matrix without changing the solution set of the system it represents.

concepts.name: Ensemble Learning
concepts.definition: Combining several models so their errors partly cancel and the whole beats any part.

concepts.name: Cauchy (ε–δ) Definition of a Limit
concepts.definition: The formal definition: for every ε there is a δ such that arguments within δ of the point map to values within ε of the limit.

concepts.name: Euler Diagram
concepts.definition: A picture of sets as regions, used to reason about their overlaps.

concepts.name: Event
concepts.definition: A subset of the event space, so that operations on events are operations on sets.

concepts.name: Event Space
concepts.definition: The set of all possible outcomes of an experiment, the universe in which probability is defined.

concepts.name: Expected Value
concepts.definition: The probability-weighted average of a random variable, its long-run mean.

concepts.name: F1 / Dice Score
concepts.definition: The harmonic mean of precision and recall, a single number balancing the two.

concepts.name: Feed-Forward Network
concepts.definition: A network of neuron layers passing signals in one direction from input to output.

concepts.name: Graphing Functions
concepts.definition: Assembling limits, derivatives and convexity into a full qualitative picture of a function's graph.

concepts.name: Jordan–Gauss Method (Gaussian Elimination)
concepts.definition: The systematic procedure of applying elementary row operations to bring a matrix to row-echelon form, and thereby to solve a system of linear equations by a fixed algorithm rather than ad-hoc tricks.

concepts.name: Geometric Transformations as Matrices
concepts.definition: The correspondence between matrices and geometric motions of the plane: applying a matrix to the coordinate vectors of a figure moves the figure, so composing motions becomes multiplying matrices.

concepts.name: Heine (Sequential) Definition of a Limit
concepts.definition: An equivalent definition of a function limit stated through the limits of all sequences approaching the point.

concepts.name: Hierarchical Clustering
concepts.definition: Building a nested tree of clusters by repeatedly merging or splitting groups.

concepts.name: Higher-Order Derivative
concepts.definition: The result of differentiating repeatedly; the second derivative measures curvature.

concepts.name: Holistic View of Evaluation
concepts.definition: Judging a model by the whole picture of metrics, baselines and error structure rather than one score.

concepts.name: Improper Integral
concepts.definition: An integral over an unbounded interval or of an unbounded function, defined as a limit of ordinary integrals.

concepts.name: Indefinite Integral
concepts.definition: The family of all antiderivatives of a function, differing by a constant.

concepts.name: Independent Events
concepts.definition: Events where knowing one occurred does not change the probability of the other.

concepts.name: Integration by Parts
concepts.definition: Trading one integral for another using the product rule in reverse.

concepts.name: Integration by Substitution
concepts.definition: Changing variable in an integral so that it matches a known antiderivative; the chain rule reversed.

concepts.name: Cauchy's Intermediate Value Theorem
concepts.definition: A function continuous on a closed interval attains every value between its endpoint values.

concepts.name: Explicit Inverse Formula for a 2×2 Matrix
concepts.definition: The closed-form expression that gives the inverse of a 2×2 matrix directly from its four entries and its determinant, with no elimination needed.

concepts.name: Inverse Matrix
concepts.definition: The matrix that undoes another: multiplying a matrix by its inverse gives the identity. It exists only for square matrices that are non-degenerate.

concepts.name: Finding an Inverse by the Jordan–Gauss Method
concepts.definition: Computing an inverse by row-reducing the matrix alongside the identity until the original becomes the identity and the identity becomes the inverse.

concepts.name: K-Means
concepts.definition: Partitioning data into k clusters by alternately assigning points to nearest centroids and recomputing them.

concepts.name: K-Nearest Neighbours
concepts.definition: Predicting from the labels of the closest training examples, with no explicit training step.

concepts.name: L1 Regularization
concepts.definition: Penalising the sum of absolute weights, which drives some exactly to zero and selects features.

concepts.name: L2 Regularization
concepts.definition: Penalising the sum of squared weights, shrinking them smoothly toward zero.

concepts.name: Lagrange Mean Value Theorem
concepts.definition: On any interval a differentiable function has a point whose derivative equals the average rate of change across the interval.

concepts.name: L'Hôpital's Rule
concepts.definition: A technique for evaluating indeterminate limits by differentiating numerator and denominator separately.

concepts.name: Limit of a Function at a Point
concepts.definition: The value a function approaches as its argument approaches a given point, independently of the value at that point.

concepts.name: Limit of a Sequence
concepts.definition: The value a sequence approaches arbitrarily closely as the index grows without bound.

concepts.name: Linear Equation
concepts.definition: An equation in which every unknown appears only to the first power and is not multiplied by another unknown. It is the atom the whole course is built from.

concepts.name: Thinking in Terms of Linear Models
concepts.definition: The habit the course is ultimately aiming at: recognising when a situation with many quantities changing at once can be posed and solved linearly, rather than memorising procedures.

concepts.name: Linear Regression
concepts.definition: Fitting a linear function of the features by minimising squared error.

concepts.name: Linear Space (Vector Space)
concepts.definition: The abstract setting in which addition and scalar multiplication obey a fixed list of rules; recognising it is what lets the same reasoning transfer from arrows to data tables to functions.

concepts.name: Little-o Notation
concepts.definition: A notation stating that one function is asymptotically negligible relative to another.

concepts.name: Logical Operations
concepts.definition: Negation, conjunction, disjunction and implication, which combine propositions into compound statements.

concepts.name: Logical Proposition
concepts.definition: A statement that is definitely either true or false, the atom of formal reasoning.

concepts.name: Maclaurin Series
concepts.definition: The Taylor series taken at zero.

concepts.name: Matrix
concepts.definition: A rectangular table of numbers arranged in rows and columns, used to store coefficients, data sets or transformations compactly.

concepts.name: Matrix Addition
concepts.definition: Adding two matrices of identical dimensions entry by entry.

concepts.name: Modelling Real Situations with Vectors and Matrices
concepts.definition: The practice of translating a real problem — a small economic balance, a data-analysis task — into vectors and matrices so that it becomes a solvable system.

concepts.name: Matrix Multiplication
concepts.definition: Combining two matrices into a third whose entries are dot products of rows with columns; it corresponds to performing one transformation after another and is not commutative.

concepts.name: Matrix Transposition
concepts.definition: Reflecting a matrix across its main diagonal so that rows become columns; the operation behind symmetric matrices and many identities.

concepts.name: Matrix–Vector Multiplication
concepts.definition: Applying a matrix to a vector to obtain a new vector; this is the operation that turns a matrix into a transformation and lets an SLE be written as a single equation.

concepts.name: Mean Value Theorem for Integrals
concepts.definition: A continuous function attains its average value over an interval at some interior point.

concepts.name: Multiplication Rule
concepts.definition: When choices are made in sequence, the number of outcomes is the product of the counts.

concepts.name: Building Negations to Claims
concepts.definition: Turning a statement, including quantified ones, into its correct denial — the skill behind complementary events.

concepts.name: Newton–Leibniz Formula
concepts.definition: The fundamental link: a definite integral equals the increment of any antiderivative across the interval.

concepts.name: t-SNE / UMAP
concepts.definition: Non-linear dimensionality reduction aimed at preserving local neighbourhoods for visualisation.

concepts.name: The Number e
concepts.definition: The limit of (1+1/n)^n, the base of the natural exponential and logarithm.

concepts.name: One-Sided Limit
concepts.definition: The limit taken as the argument approaches a point from only the left or only the right.

concepts.name: Overfitting
concepts.definition: Fitting noise in the training data so that performance on unseen data degrades.

concepts.name: Principal Component Analysis
concepts.definition: Projecting data onto the directions of greatest variance, found from the eigenstructure of its covariance matrix.

concepts.name: Permutation
concepts.definition: An arrangement of objects where order matters.

concepts.name: A Posteriori Probability
concepts.definition: The updated probability of a hypothesis after evidence has been observed.

concepts.name: Power Series
concepts.definition: A series in powers of the variable, which behaves like a polynomial inside its region of convergence.

concepts.name: Precision
concepts.definition: The share of predicted positives that are actually positive.

concepts.name: Probability
concepts.definition: A number between 0 and 1 assigned to an event, measuring how likely it is.

concepts.name: Rules of Probability
concepts.definition: The axioms and their consequences: complement, addition for unions, monotonicity.

concepts.name: Random Distribution
concepts.definition: The assignment of probabilities to the values a random variable can take.

concepts.name: Random Forest
concepts.definition: Bagged decision trees with additional random feature subsampling at each split.

concepts.name: Random Variable
concepts.definition: A numerical quantity whose value is determined by the outcome of a random experiment.

concepts.name: Recall
concepts.definition: The share of truly positive cases the model retrieves.

concepts.name: Reflection (Symmetry)
concepts.definition: A transformation mirroring the plane across a line, expressible as a matrix and reversing orientation.

concepts.name: Regression
concepts.definition: Supervised prediction of a continuous numeric value.

concepts.name: Regularization
concepts.definition: Deliberately constraining a model to reduce overfitting at the cost of some training fit.

concepts.name: ROC / AUC
concepts.definition: The curve of true against false positive rates over all thresholds, and the area beneath it.

concepts.name: Rolle's Theorem
concepts.definition: A function continuous on a closed interval, differentiable inside it and equal at the endpoints has a stationary point strictly inside.

concepts.name: Rotation
concepts.definition: A transformation turning the plane about a point by a fixed angle, expressible as a matrix built from sine and cosine.

concepts.name: Row-Echelon Form
concepts.definition: A staircase shape for a matrix in which each leading entry sits strictly to the right of the one above it, making the solution of the corresponding system readable almost directly.

concepts.name: Scalar Multiplication
concepts.definition: Multiplying every entry of a vector or matrix by the same number, which stretches, shrinks or flips it without changing its shape.

concepts.name: Scaling
concepts.definition: A transformation stretching or shrinking the plane along its axes, the simplest case of a matrix acting geometrically.

concepts.name: Second Derivative Test
concepts.definition: Classifying a stationary point as a minimum or maximum by the sign of the second derivative there.

concepts.name: Sequence
concepts.definition: An ordered infinite list of numbers indexed by the natural numbers.

concepts.name: Series
concepts.definition: The formal sum of infinitely many terms, studied through the limit of its partial sums.

concepts.name: Set
concepts.definition: A collection of distinct objects considered as one whole.

concepts.name: Set Operations
concepts.definition: Union, intersection, difference and complement, the operations mirrored later by operations on events.

concepts.name: Solution Set of an SLE
concepts.definition: The full set of assignments satisfying a system: it may be empty, a single point, or an infinite family, and which case holds can be read off the row-echelon form.
concepts.aliases: consistency of a system|solutions for SLE

concepts.name: Solving an SLE via the Inverse Matrix
concepts.definition: Writing a square system as a single matrix equation and solving it by multiplying both sides by the inverse — an alternative strategy to elimination.

concepts.name: Special Limits
concepts.definition: The small catalogue of standard limits that serve as building blocks for evaluating harder ones.

concepts.name: Special Matrices
concepts.definition: Named matrix shapes that behave in particular ways — identity, zero, diagonal, square, symmetric — which act as the reference points for later operations.

concepts.name: Stacking and Blending
concepts.definition: Training a further model to combine the predictions of the base models.

concepts.name: Standard Deviation
concepts.definition: The square root of the variance, expressing spread in the units of the variable.

concepts.name: Subset
concepts.definition: A set all of whose elements belong to another set.

concepts.name: Supervised Learning
concepts.definition: Learning a mapping from inputs to known target values using labelled examples.

concepts.name: System of Linear Equations (SLE)
concepts.definition: A finite collection of linear equations that must hold simultaneously for the same set of unknowns; a solution is any assignment of values satisfying all of them at once.

concepts.name: Taylor Series
concepts.definition: The power series generated by a function's derivatives at a point.

concepts.name: Taylor's Formula
concepts.definition: An approximation of a smooth function near a point by a polynomial built from its derivatives, with a controlled remainder.

concepts.name: Total Probability Law
concepts.definition: Decomposing an event's probability across a partition of the event space; the chain rule of probability.

concepts.name: Train/Validation Split
concepts.definition: Holding out part of the data to estimate performance on examples not used for fitting.

concepts.name: Training Loop
concepts.definition: The repeated cycle of forward pass, loss evaluation, gradient computation and weight update.

concepts.name: Truth Table
concepts.definition: An exhaustive table of a compound statement's value for every assignment of its parts.

concepts.name: Unsupervised Learning
concepts.definition: Finding structure in data without target labels.

concepts.name: Variance
concepts.definition: The expected squared deviation from the mean, measuring spread.

concepts.name: Vector
concepts.definition: An ordered tuple of numbers treated as a single algebraic object that can be added to another vector and scaled by a number; geometrically an arrow with direction and length.

concepts.name: Vector Addition
concepts.definition: Adding two vectors componentwise to produce a third vector of the same size.

concepts.name: Weierstrass's Theorem
concepts.definition: A function continuous on a closed bounded interval is bounded and attains a maximum and a minimum on it.

concepts.name: Weight Decay
concepts.definition: Shrinking weights at every update step, the optimisation-side view of L2 penalty.
